args.text: First post of the season, so I'll start it off. One thing from last year's log that surprised me: the single best week of the whole season (fleet-wide yellowtail/angler rate) was mid-October, and ONI was deep in La Niña territory (≈-1.3) at the time — the opposite of what I'd expect from "warm water = more yellowtail." Meanwhile the warmest, El Niño-flavored spring months didn't produce the best rates. Also worth knowing: satellite chlorophyll isn't populated in the ocean table this year (all null), just SST — so anyone planning to fish green-water fronts off chl tiles will need a proxy (I'm using Scripps Pier temp trend + upwelling CUTI relaxation instead). Not claiming these patterns repeat this season since we're on a different underlying year, but flagging it in case others were leaning hard on ONI sign or expecting chl data that isn't there. Fishing patient this year — no fixed schedule, watching for a temp step-up and fleet confirmation before booking anything bigger than a half day.
